---
title: "🚀 Quick start"
---

With the `krsim` environment active, run the five main stages on a small example. Results go to `krsim_quickstart_output/` in the current folder (krsim creates it):

```bash
OUT=krsim_quickstart_output

krsim simulate   --Nh 3 --T 10 --K 2 --chi 0.18 --C 1 --random_seed 123 --output_dir $OUT
krsim mutate     --ts $OUT/ts_123.trees --random_seed 123 --output_dir $OUT
krsim coal-mut   --ts $OUT/ts_mut_123.trees --random_seed 123 --output_dir $OUT
krsim vcf-strain --ts $OUT/ts_mut_123.trees --random_seed 123 --output_dir $OUT
krsim vcf-host   --strain_vcf $OUT/output_123_strain.vcf --ind_node_map_csv $OUT/sim_ind_node_map_123.csv \
                 --depth 10 --random_seed 123 --output_dir $OUT
```

The `simulate` line runs 3 hosts (`--Nh`) for 10 generations (`--T`), with 2 parasites passed on per mosquito bite (`--K`), a superinfection probability of 0.18 (`--chi`) and 1 oocyst per mosquito (`--C`). See the [Stage 1 options](commands.qmd#stage-1-simulate-genealogy) for details.

Each command prints the files it wrote. Every file name ends in the random seed (`123` here), and every command adds a record of what it ran to `KR_sim_123.log`.

## What each step does

| Command | Reads | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| `simulate` | — | `ts_123.trees`, `sim_ind_node_map_123.csv` |
| `mutate` | `ts_123.trees` | `ts_mut_123.trees` |
| `coal-mut` | `ts_mut_123.trees` | `coal_T_123.csv`, `mut_T_123.csv` |
| `vcf-strain` | `ts_mut_123.trees` | `output_123_strain.vcf` |
| `vcf-host` | `output_123_strain.vcf`, `sim_ind_node_map_123.csv` | `output_123_host.vcf` |
